title: Train Interlocking Schema
description: Schema for a train interlocking: the train-domain route-control artifact (issue #1248, parent #1246). The interlocking YAML is authoritative for the guarded route space; each executable route maps to exactly one numbered linear train variant. Mermaid/SVG/coverage outputs are derived projections, never sources of truth. Core validates shape only; semantic cross-checks (digit/train agreement, lifeline resolution, guard-ref existence) and Station Master reachability live in the Python API and downstream validators.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the interlocking schema this document targets.

title.description: Human-readable display name for the interlocking.

theme.description: Kebab-case theme this interlocking belongs to (mirrors train theme semantics).

status.description: Authoring lifecycle state of the interlocking artifact.

path.description: Canonical path to this interlocking YAML relative to repo root (plan/_trains/_interlockings/<id>.yaml).

content_digest.description: sha256 (hex) of the normalized interlocking content, or a placeholder during authoring.

entrypoint.description: Declared reachability surface so extension validators never infer reachability from filenames. Core validates shape only; Station Master reachability is enforced in atdd-extensions#27.

exposed.description: Whether this interlocking is reachable via a Station Master action.

actions.description: Station Master action names (NOT train IDs) that route into this interlocking.

reason.description: Required when exposed is false; must be null when exposed is true.

strategy.description: Explicit route-resolution strategy. No implicit order-based resolution is allowed. fail_on_multiple_match fails closed when >1 route matches; first_priority picks the lowest unique numeric priority.

lifelines.description: Declared participants (sequence-diagram lifelines). Message endpoints must resolve to one of these.

ref.description: Lifeline reference: wagon:<id>, user:<role>, or system:<source>.

messages.description: Declared messages between lifelines. Carries payload contract identity only, never Cargo runtime data.

invariants.description: Declarative invariants that must hold across the interlocking.

residuals.description: Structural obligations that have no honest flow representation and are discharged by a named validator.

routes.description: Guarded routes. Each executable route maps to exactly one linear train variant whose `category` field (issue #1421) agrees with the route's declared category — no longer a matching identity digit.

category_assessment.description: Typed not-applicable assessments per route category (issue #1554). Every category in the closed set must be ASSESSED: `nominal` always requires one or more routes and can never appear here, while `alternate`, `error` and `exception` are satisfied either by routes or by a typed entry here. This replaces the weaker 'at least one non-nominal route' floor, which a token alternate satisfies while error and exception behaviour go unwritten. Declaring an entry for a category that already carries routes is a contradiction, so a stale assessment cannot outlive the gap it described.

category_assessment_entry.description: Why a category carries no route. The basis is drawn from a CLOSED vocabulary — a free-text reason is deliberately not accepted, since a prose escape hatch erodes as it gets copy-pasted onto every category.

basis.description: `discharged-by-residual` = the outcome exists but deliberately has no route, and the residual named by `residual_ref` accounts for it (that residual must itself carry a reason, an acceptance_ref and a validator_ref per planner.train.interlocking-structural-residual-explicit, so this discharge is bound, not free). `outcome-cannot-arise` = the category is impossible by construction. `not-yet-assessed` = TRANSITIONAL; the analysis has not been performed and `retires_with` must name the issue that will retire it.

residual_ref.description: The declared residual that accounts for this category. REQUIRED when basis is `discharged-by-residual` and forbidden otherwise. Must name a residual declared in this interlocking's `residuals` block.

retires_with.description: Issue number that will retire a `not-yet-assessed` basis. REQUIRED when basis is `not-yet-assessed` and forbidden otherwise, so an unassessed category is an owned obligation with a named retirer.

kind.description: boundary = between two distinct lifelines; self = a lifeline to itself; control = a control-flow note.

payload.description: Payload contract identity ONLY. Never carries Cargo runtime contents or artifact_data values.

contract.description: Payload contract identity — decided ONCE for #1410: exactly TWO segments in domain:resource form (e.g. match:result), the leaf identity the full contract:<theme>:...:<resource> URN family prefixes. A third colon segment is rejected. Null when there is no payload.

expression.description: Declarative, side-effect-free guard expression. Operators: == != < <= > >= and or not exists(field) in. No raw Python eval, no function calls except exists(), no imports/IO/mutation.
Declarative invariant expression (same grammar as guards).

validator_ref.description: Path to the validator that discharges this residual obligation.

category.description: The route's variant classification. Judged by comparing it against the `category` FIELD of the target train (planner.train.interlocking-route-category-matches-train-id) — never against a digit parsed out of the identity. The `category_digit` key it replaced is RETIRED (issues #1421, #1440) and is now rejected outright.

priority.description: Numeric priority. Under first_priority resolution, priorities must be unique.

guard_ref.description: Reference to a guard declared in fragments[].guards[].

train_id.description: Target linear train this route selects: typed train:<subject>:<slug> (issue #1421), or the legacy NNNN-slug form during the migration transition.

train_path.description: Canonical path to the target train YAML (plan/_trains/<train_id>.yaml).

expected_sequence_digest.description: sha256 (hex) of the normalized route projection (the target train's linear sequence over the projected fields).

fields.description: Ordered projection fields. Defaults to [step, intent, from, to, artifact] when omitted.
